items.passage: As Lisbeth talks, her voice carries him back to the past. Unconsciously she has fallen into an attitude which is as familiar as all the rest, her hands folded on her knees, her face turned seaward. The scent of the sea is in the air; the sound of its murmurs in his ears. The color on the usually clear, pale cheek is the color he used to admire with such lover-like extravagance--a pure pink tint, bright and rare. She seems to have gone back to her seventeen years, and he has gone back with her.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show how Lisbeth's familiar posture and appearance draw the man back into memories of their youth
To explain why Lisbeth refuses to look at the man while she is speaking
To describe a sudden storm rising over the sea as Lisbeth talks
To argue that the man no longer admires anything about Lisbeth's looks
items.explanation: 지문은 리스베스의 목소리가 그를 과거로 데려간다는 첫 문장과, 손을 무릎에 포갠 익숙한 자세·뺨의 분홍빛을 묘사하는 문장들로 회상을 전개한다. 마지막 문장도 둘이 함께 열일곱 살로 돌아간 듯하다고 정리하므로 A가 서술 목적에 맞다. B는 바다 쪽을 향한 얼굴을 거부로 잘못 해석했다. C의 폭풍은 지문에 없고, D는 그가 그 빛깔을 열렬히 찬미했다는 내용과 반대다.

items.passage:
A course of reading can hardly be prescribed for all ladies. But it should be remarked, that this sex cannot be too well acquainted with the writers upon human life and manners. The Spectator should fill the first place in every lady's library. Other volumes of periodical papers, tho inferior to the Spectator, should be read; and some of the best histories.

With respect to novels, so much admired by the young, and so generally condemned by the old, what shall I say? Perhaps it may be said with truth, that some of them are useful, many of them pernicious, and most of them trifling.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Young women should avoid all books except histories and periodical papers.
Women should read widely about human life and manners, though novels deserve caution.
Novels are the most valuable reading for young people because they are admired.
Older readers are wrong to condemn novels that the young enjoy.
items.explanation: 필자는 여성이 인간의 삶과 풍속을 다룬 작가들을 아무리 잘 알아도 지나치지 않다고 하며 정기 간행물과 역사서를 권한다. 이어 소설에 대해서는 일부는 유익하나 다수는 해롭고 대부분은 하찮다고 평가하므로 B가 요지다. A는 '모든 책을 피하라'로 지나치게 단정한다. C와 D는 소설에 대한 필자의 유보적 태도와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: All this was not unnoticed by Mr. Beecher, as we realised one day when, as he entered the pulpit, he turned to Mr. Whitney, on duty there, and putting his hand to his ear quietly said, "I am very hard of hearing, can you not give me a front seat?" Others, if you give them a front seat, say it tires their eyes to look up, and if they are seated too far back, they cannot see. It is the duty of the usher to satisfy all. That strangers come so constantly is witness to the cordiality and courtesy of their reception and treatment.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
options: To criticize Mr. Beecher for demanding special treatment in the church
To explain why strangers rarely return to the church after one visit
To illustrate the challenges ushers face in seating people and the welcome they offer
To describe how Mr. Whitney lost his hearing while on duty
items.explanation: 지문은 비처 씨가 앞자리를 요청한 일화와, 앞자리는 눈이 피곤하고 뒷자리는 안 보인다는 다른 사람들의 불평을 나열한 뒤 '모두를 만족시키는 것이 안내원의 의무'라고 말한다. 마지막에는 낯선 이들이 계속 오는 것이 친절한 응대의 증거라고 하므로 C가 목적이다. A는 일화가 가볍고 유머러스하게 제시된 점을 놓친다. B는 지문과 반대이고, D는 청력을 잃은 사람을 잘못 짚었다.

items.passage:
There was no cotton to be found. She then began to search for it amongst the grass, but it was so thick and tall that there was little chance of so small a thing as a reel of cotton being recovered when once lost in it. At length, after nearly an hour's ineffectual search, she returned to the cottage.

What should she do? The lost reel of cotton was the only one her mother possessed. Mrs. Gordon had sent several reels of cotton with the shirts, as she was most particular as to the cotton that was used; and Katie had heard her mother say she hoped there would be sufficient to finish the set, as she could not get any more like it in the village.
items.question: Based on the text, why is Katie so troubled after her search?
options: The lost reel was her mother's only one, and suitable cotton could not be bought in the village.
She fears Mrs. Gordon will refuse to send any more shirts to the cottage.
She dislikes searching in the thick grass and wants to avoid more chores.
Her mother had warned her never to take the cotton outside.
items.explanation: 지문은 잃어버린 실패가 어머니가 가진 유일한 것이었다고 밝히고, 고든 부인이 실에 까다로워 마을에서는 같은 실을 구할 수 없다는 어머니의 말을 덧붙인다. 그래서 A가 카티의 고민 이유다. B의 셔츠 주문 중단은 언급되지 않는다. C는 한 시간 가까이 찾은 노력과 맞지 않고, D의 경고는 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
A word, a lick and a click and--yes, wonderful to relate, the flag falls! Off? Yes, really off! Whoever saw a better go! Away they speed, neck and neck!

Two mile heats! Breathless, the people lean forward to watch them, as they grow dimmer in the distance. Now on they come! As they near the quarter-stretch they still keep together, and pass beneath the string in the same order. So far, it is a beautiful race. Again they come! Men and boys shout wildly as they see a gap, a little gap, when they turn once more.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Somber and mournful
Excited and breathless
Detached and analytical
Bitter and accusatory
items.explanation: 'wonderful to relate', 'Whoever saw a better go!' 같은 감탄문과 짧은 문장들이 경주의 긴박함을 전한다. 사람들이 숨죽여 몸을 내밀고 남자와 소년들이 거칠게 소리친다는 묘사도 흥분된 분위기를 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A의 슬픔, C의 냉정한 분석, D의 비난은 지문 어디에도 드러나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Though I was bitterly angry with Fay--though I found it impossible to excuse or condone her cruel behaviour towards me, her husband--I nevertheless loved and longed for her with consuming and increasing force. "Let no man dream but that I loved her still": therein lay the bitterest sting of my agony. The more I loved her the more impossible I found it to forgive her: had I cared for her less, I might have been less implacable. That may not be a symptom of ideal love, but anyway it was a symptom of mine.

But if I found it impossible to forgive Fay, I found it still further out of my power to forgive Frank.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the narrator's feelings toward Fay?
options: He has forgiven her completely and no longer feels any anger.
He feels indifferent to her and cares only about Frank.
He loves her intensely even while he cannot forgive her.
He pities her but has stopped loving her.
items.explanation: 화자는 페이에게 몹시 화가 났고 그녀의 행동을 용서할 수 없다고 하면서도 그녀를 '점점 더 강하게' 사랑했다고 말한다. 또 사랑할수록 용서가 더 불가능했다고 고백하므로 C가 관계를 정확히 나타낸다. A는 용서했다는 점에서 틀리다. B와 D는 화자가 여전히 그녀를 사랑한다는 진술과 모순된다.

items.passage: A sense of all that he had escaped in not having had to live with her rolled over him like a wave, while he looked strangely at Mr. Roy, to whom this privilege had been vouchsafed. He saw in a moment his successor had a constitution that would carry it. Mr. Roy suggested squareness and solidity; he was a broadbased, comfortable, polished man, with a surface in which the rank tendrils of irritation would not easily obtain a foothold. He had a broad, blank face, a capacious mouth, and a small, light eye, to which, as he entered, he was engaged in adjusting a double gold-rimmed glass.
items.question: In the text, Mr. Roy's broad, smooth, polished surface most likely represents
options: his deep sorrow over a recent loss
his eagerness to argue with strangers
his poor eyesight and physical weakness
his ability to endure her irritations without being troubled
items.explanation: 주인공은 그녀와 함께 살지 않아도 되었던 것에 안도하면서, 후계자인 로이 씨가 그것을 견딜 체질을 가졌다고 본다. 이어 로이 씨의 매끈한 표면에는 '짜증의 덩굴'이 쉽게 뿌리내리지 못한다고 묘사하므로 D가 상징 의미다. A의 슬픔이나 B의 논쟁 성향은 근거가 없다. C는 안경을 맞추는 동작을 과잉 해석했다.

items.passage:
Taking the bellows in hand she blew furiously, and was presently rewarded with a brisk blaze. She smiled with satisfaction, and trotted upstairs to find her red knit shawl. With this about her shoulders she was prepared to brave the December frost. Down the steps she went, and deposited the ark discreetly at their foot; then returned to take up her position behind the curtains.

There were a good many people passing, but they seemed too preoccupied to glance down at the sidewalk. They were nearly all hurrying in one direction. Some were running in the middle of the street.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “brave the December frost” most nearly suggests that the woman
options: prepares herself to face the cold outside
refuses to leave the warm house
complains loudly about the winter weather
forgets that the season has turned cold
items.explanation: 그녀는 불을 지핀 뒤 빨간 숄을 어깨에 두르고서야 12월의 서리를 '맞설' 준비가 되었다. 곧바로 계단을 내려가 밖에 상자를 두고 오므로, 이 구절은 추위 속으로 나갈 각오를 뜻하는 A다. B는 그녀가 실제로 밖에 나간 사실과 어긋난다. C의 불평과 D의 망각은 지문에 드러나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Each morning, as soon as the bugle call was sounded, he would take his place in line with the other patients, advance to his turn, and receive the usual treatment. This habit continued until the wound was healed. Always, after this, to every friendly greeting, he would respond by holding up the wounded leg for inspection, and he acted as though he thought that everybody was interested in the honorable scar that told the story of patriotic duty faithfully performed.

Later on, for some reason known to himself, Carlo transferred his special allegiance to Co. K, and maintained close connection with that Company until the end of his term of service. He was regarded by its members as a member of the Company mess, and was treated as one of them.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “transferred his special allegiance” most nearly suggests that Carlo
options: was moved to another hospital by his doctors
chose to attach himself loyally to a different company
lost interest in all the soldiers around him
was punished for leaving his place in line
items.explanation: 카를로는 이전에 환자들과 줄을 서서 치료를 받았지만, 이후 K 중대에 '특별한 충성'을 옮겨 복무 끝까지 그 중대와 가까이 지냈다. 중대원들도 그를 식사 동료로 대했다는 서술이 근거이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 병원 이동으로 오해했다. C는 그가 친밀한 관계를 유지한 사실과 반대이고, D의 처벌은 언급되지 않는다.

items.passage:
Rushes that grow by the black water
When will I see you more?
When will the sorrowful heart forget you,
Land of the green, green shore?
When will the field and the small cabin
See us more
In the old country?

What is to me all the gold yonder?
She that bore me is gone.
Knees that dandled and hands that blessed me
Colder than any stone;
Stranger to me than the face of strangers
Are my own
In the old country.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “Colder than any stone” most nearly suggests that the speaker's mother
options: was strict and unkind to her child
lives in a harsh, wintry place
has died and is beyond the speaker's reach
no longer remembers the speaker
items.explanation: 화자는 '나를 낳은 이가 떠났다'고 말한 뒤, 자신을 어르고 축복하던 무릎과 손이 어떤 돌보다 차갑다고 표현한다. 이는 어머니의 죽음을 뜻하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '축복하던 손'과 맞지 않는다. B는 실제 날씨로 오해했고, D는 기억 상실을 말하는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: A single tree was tinged with glory from the west, and threw a pensive shade behind. Not far from where it fell was the tomb of my parents, whom I had hardly thought of in bidding adieu to the village, but had remembered them more faithfully among the feelings that drew me homeward. At my departure their tomb had been hidden in the morning mist. Beholding it in the sunshine now, I felt a sensation through my frame as if a breeze had thrown the coolness of September over me, though not a leaf was stirred, nor did the thistle-down take flight.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “thrown the coolness of September over me” most nearly suggests that the narrator
options: was chilled because a strong wind began to blow
felt the season change suddenly around the village
regretted leaving the village in the autumn
experienced a sudden shiver of feeling at the sight of the tomb
items.explanation: 화자는 햇빛 속 부모의 무덤을 보며 몸에 어떤 감각이 지나갔다고 하고, 잎 하나 흔들리지 않았다고 덧붙인다. 즉 실제 바람이 아닌 감정의 전율을 비유한 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A와 B는 바람·계절을 문자 그대로 읽었다. C의 후회는 귀향의 감정과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: The purpose of the ministry filled him with shame and indignation. Confronted abruptly with the course which four months before had seemed to him natural and proper, the shock brought out the fulness of the change through which he had passed meantime. He has no illusions about Corsica. The inhabitants had disappointed all the expectations of the British,--"At a peace I should rejoice at having given up the island." But the days passing over his head had brought wider and maturer views of the general policy of Great Britain, as well as increasing faith in the powers of the fleet, vigorously used in aggressive warfare.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the days passing over his head” most nearly suggests
options: the gradual passing of time that broadened his understanding
a series of storms that damaged the fleet
the many orders he received from the ministry
the burden of his growing age and illness
items.explanation: 지문은 그가 넉 달 전에는 자연스럽다고 여긴 방침에 이제 수치를 느낄 만큼 변했다고 한다. 이어 '머리 위로 지나간 날들'이 더 넓고 성숙한 견해와 함대에 대한 믿음을 가져왔다고 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 폭풍으로 잘못 읽었다. C의 명령과 D의 노화·질병은 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Now, down to a moment ago, we had never been able to understand for what possible ______ a great number of odd, lazy, large-headed men, whom one is in the habit of meeting here, and there, and everywhere, could ever have been created. We see it all, now. They are the supernumeraries in the pantomime of life; the men who have been thrust into it, with no other view than to be constantly tumbling over each other, and running their heads against all sorts of strange things. We sat opposite to one of these men at a supper-table, only last week.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: harm
purpose
delay
rumor
items.explanation: 화자는 이상한 사람들이 '무슨 목적으로' 창조되었는지 몰랐다가 이제 알겠다고 말한다. 이어 그들이 삶의 무언극에서 서로 넘어지기 위해서만 존재하는 단역이라고 설명하므로 빈칸에는 B가 들어가야 한다. A, C, D는 '창조된 이유'라는 문맥에 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
More than this, a bright beam of sunlight now shone through the dusty window. Sobbing no longer, she carefully wrapped the doll in the same paper and piece of silk that had held it for so many years. As she arose, holding the parcel in her hand, the pink dress and black silk apron on her lap fell to the floor.

A sudden thought came to her. Dorry never could remain ______ very long at a time. She hastily opened the parcel again.

"Lie down there, Delia dear," she said, gently placing the doll on the rose-buds of the still open trunk-lid. "Lie down there, till I put on these things. I'm going to take you down to see your uncle!"
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: proud
hungry
sad
asleep
items.explanation: 도리는 방금까지 흐느끼다가 이제 울음을 멈추고, 갑자기 떠오른 생각에 즐겁게 인형을 데려가려 한다. 그러므로 '오래 슬퍼할 수 없는' 아이라는 C가 맞다. A, B, D는 울음을 그친 뒤 기분이 바뀌는 흐름과 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage: The autumn will afford us the best opportunity for observation. At that season the spider-egg tufts are turning out their baby spiders by the millions, each a perfect grown spider in miniature, and apparently as skilled at birth in the peculiar arts of its kind as its parents were in their ripe old age. Here is a troop of them upon this drooping branch of wild grape by the river brink. Its leaves are glistening in the loose, rambling tangle which marks their wanderings. They are evidently not satisfied with their present surroundings, and would seem desirous of getting as far as possible from the neighborhood of their cradle and swaddling-clothes. They are the most ______ and self-reliant babies on record.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: helpless
sleepy
timid
independent
items.explanation: 새끼 거미들은 태어날 때부터 부모만큼 능숙하고, 요람에서 최대한 멀어지려 한다고 묘사된다. 빈칸 뒤 'self-reliant'와도 짝을 이루므로 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 스스로 멀리 떠나는 모습과 반대된다.

items.passage: The flowers sent to me by kind neighbours have not perished,--that is, the idea and pleasure of them remain, though every blossom was withered months ago. The game and fruit, eaten in their season, remain as comforts and luxuries, preserved in the love that sent them. Every letter and conversation abides,--every new idea is mine for ever; all the knowledge, all the experience of the year, is so much gain. Even the courses of the planets, and the changes of the moon, and the hay-making and harvest, are so much immortal wealth--as real a possession as all the pain of the year was a ______ apparition. Yes, even the quick bursts of sunshine are still mine.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: passing
permanent
cherished
shared
items.explanation: 필자는 기쁨과 지식은 영원히 남는 재산이지만, 한 해의 고통은 그것과 대조된다고 말한다. 꽃은 시들어도 기쁨은 남는다는 앞 문장과 함께 보면 고통은 '지나가는' 환영이므로 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 고통을 남는 것으로 만들어 대조를 깨고, D는 문맥과 무관하다.

items.passage: The boys would have lots of chance for wholesome play as well as drill, and would get no end of fun out of it. The possible hardships of camping out would have no existence for them. As for any lasting good to come of it, outside of physical benefits, I think the discipline alone, with what it stands for, would cover that. In the reform schools, where they have military drill, they have found it their most ______ ally in dealing with the worst and wildest class of the boys. It is the bump of organization that is touched again there.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: reluctant
useful
costly
distant
items.explanation: 필자는 훈련의 규율이 소년들에게 지속적인 이익을 준다고 주장하고, 소년원에서도 군사 훈련을 쓴다고 예를 든다. 가장 거친 소년들을 다룰 때 도움이 되었다는 문맥이므로 B가 들어가야 한다. A, C, D는 훈련을 긍정하는 필자의 논지와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Only by slow degrees did I realise that I was not in my comfortable bed at home, but in a chilly, ill-lighted railway-carriage. Chilly--yes, that it was--very chilly; but as my faculties returned I remembered my precious bag, and forgot all else in a momentary terror that it had been taken from me. No; there it was--my elbow had been pressed against it as I slept. But how was this? The train was not in motion. We were standing in a station; a dingy deserted-looking place, with no cheerful noise or bustle; only one or two porters slowly moving about, with a sort of sleepy "night duty," surly air.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in the text?
options: From drowsy confusion to sudden alarm, then to uneasy observation of a gloomy station
From cheerful excitement to calm relief as the narrator reaches home
From anger at the porters to gratitude for their help
From fear of theft to amusement at a mistaken journey
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 집 침대가 아님을 서서히 깨닫는 몽롱한 상태였다가, 가방을 빼앗겼을까 하는 순간적 공포로 바뀐다. 가방을 확인한 뒤에는 기차가 멈춘 어둡고 황량한 역을 불안하게 살펴보므로 A가 정답이다. B는 집에 도착하지 않았으므로 틀렸다. C와 D의 감사나 즐거움은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
The heartfelt emotion which thrilled in these words would have softened a woman less self-willed, less hardened in her own caprices than Lady Sarah. As it was, she was only frightened, not touched to tenderness. It was he who was ashamed of the feelings which threatened to overpower him.

Ashamed of his own weakness, and fearing that he was only irritating instead of softening her, he suddenly let her go, and raising her hand to his lips, pressed one tender kiss upon it and then, turning sharply away, felt in his pocket for the keys of his gallery and went out of the study.

Lady Sarah listened a few moments, until she heard the key turn in the gallery door, and knew that her husband had shut himself in with his treasures for the evening.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone changes over the course of the text?
options: It moves from playful teasing to joyful reconciliation.
It moves from intense emotion to a quiet, lonely withdrawal.
It moves from cold anger to open celebration.
It moves from calm description to a violent quarrel.
items.explanation: 처음에는 남편의 말에 담긴 진심 어린 감정과 그를 압도하려는 감정이 강하게 드러난다. 그러나 그는 갑자기 그녀를 놓고 서재를 나가 화랑에 혼자 틀어박히며, 사라는 열쇠 소리만 듣는다. 따라서 B가 어조 변화에 맞다. A와 C는 화해·축하가 없으므로 틀렸고, D의 격렬한 다툼도 없다.

items.passage:
I have said much in praise of gentleness. I cannot say too much. Its effects are beyond calculation, both on the affections and the understanding. The victims of oppression and abuse are generally stupid, as well as selfish and hard-hearted. How can we wonder at it? They are all the time excited to evil passions, and nobody encourages what is good in them. We might as well expect flowers to grow amid the cold and storms of winter.

But gentleness, important as it is, is not all that is required in education. There should be united with it firmness--great firmness. Commands should be reasonable, and given in perfect kindness; but once given, it should be known that they must be obeyed.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in the text?
options: The author abandons praise of gentleness and argues that it harms children.
The author turns from instruction to a personal story about childhood.
The author moves from warm praise of gentleness to a firmer insistence on obedience.
The author shifts from discussing winter flowers to discussing schools.
items.explanation: 첫 단락에서 필자는 온화함의 효과가 헤아릴 수 없다며 따뜻하게 칭찬한다. 둘째 단락의 'But' 이후 온화함만으로는 부족하고 큰 단호함이 함께해야 하며 명령은 반드시 지켜져야 한다고 말하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 필자가 온화함을 여전히 중요하다고 한 점과 어긋난다. B의 개인 일화는 없고, D는 겨울 꽃 비유를 실제 주제로 오해했다.
